doc:
Row 3 — "average open price" (`avgPx`): the charge convertor's quote leaf,
rounded in the direction the position leans. Unit suffix comes from

The direction ternary is native's `side == Buy ? .down : .up`, i.e.
**Buy ⇒ [`RoundingMode::Down`]** (toward zero) and **everything else ⇒
[`RoundingMode::Up`]** (away from zero). Price is non-negative, so this row
renders identically either way; it follows the table so the file carries one
rule.

⚠️ **[`PositionDirection::Undetermined`] falls into the `.up` branch.**
Native's ternary only tests `isEqualToString:` against Buy, so a nil / unknown
side is NOT a third case — it rounds up like a Sell. Copied deliberately: a
symmetric "undetermined ⇒ nearest" would show a different price than native
on exactly the rows (unrecognised `posCcy` / `posSide`) where a parity bug is
hardest to notice.

fields.name: muted
fields.doc:
Render this tag de-emphasised: the host should substitute the neutral/grey style for the
tone's usual one, while keeping everything else about the tone (notably the voucher tone's
coupon glyph, which Android keys off `tone == Voucher`).

Deliberately presentational rather than named for the one condition that currently sets it.
The producers are the spot-grid and contract-grid overview voucher tags, muted when the
voucher is expired AND the host is in Lite mode (see `voucher_tag_is_muted` in
`grid/common/voucher_tag.rs` and the ONSHORE-ONLY note at each call site).

ANDROID-ONLY TODAY — do NOT read this as a cross-platform guarantee. Rust owns the decision,
but only Android consumes it. These tag Records appear NOWHERE in the iOS codebase: iOS's
Rust-migrated overview tab rebuilds its chips from the ObjC `infoModel` rather than from this
strip, and its voucher chip (`OKTNMPVoucherView`) is hardcoded bright and tappable and HIDES
an expired voucher outright. So setting `muted` greys the chip on Android and changes nothing
on iOS: the two platforms CAN and today DO drift. Closing that gap is an iOS-side change
(consume this strip, or mute `OKTNMPVoucherView`), not something this field can force.

This is NOT about interactivity — that is `enabled` plus `intent`. The two axes are genuinely
orthogonal: a muted tag may still be tappable (the contract twin is), and an inert tag may
still be muted.

DO NOT read "inert" as "never muted" — on spot grid the exact opposite holds. All three chips
this type emits with `intent: None, enabled: false` are inert (trailing `detail.rs:3312`,
copy/lead `:3327`, voucher `:3354`), and the VOUCHER one is the SOLE producer of a true `muted`
here: every other construction hardcodes `muted: false`. A host that keyed its muted styling
off `enabled`/`intent`, or skipped the muted branch for inert tags, would therefore skip the
only spot-grid chip that is ever muted — i.e. exactly the greying this field exists to carry.

Defaulted so adding it does not break existing generated bindings or callers that predate it.

name: bot_seekbar_amount
doc:
Percent-seek-bar amount for a bot create form: `floor(ratio * available, digit)`.

Ports `percent.mulS(quoteMax, marginDigit)` in
`RustSignalBotCreateFragment.refreshMarginView`. The widget emits a FRACTION
in [0,1], not 0-100 — `grid/common/adjust_investment.rs::amount_from_ratio`
documents the same zero-to-one contract — so the ratio is clamped, never
divided by 100.

ROUNDING IS INFERRED, not read: `com.okinc.core.ktx.mulS` is binary-only in
this workspace, and no call site in the module passes an explicit mode, so
`:642` uses the default. DOWN is taken from three converging ports —
`formatHundredfold` = `mulS(100, 2, isNoZero = false, DOWN)`
(`format_util.rs`), contract DCA's `percent.mulS(maxAmt)` implemented as
`round(precision, Down)` (`contract_dca/adjust_margin.rs`), and a bare
`mulS(sum)` ported as `round(16, Down)` (`format_util.rs`) — plus the
structural argument that an amount derived from AVAILABLE BALANCE must not
round up past it (a 100% drag has to stay within max). Confirm the last
decimal on device before treating this as settled.

Empty/unparseable available or a missing balance yields `""`, matching the
legacy path where the seek bar cannot produce a number yet.

fields.doc:

instrument, size-unit setting, role, and the legacy
`targetUnitPrecision == -1` sentinel (which means "use the contract-value
face precision" and must never reach native).

It does NOT include the `magnitude_override` ladder. That ladder keys on
the RAW per-value magnitude, so it cannot be folded into a per-convertor
number — native applies it at render step 1. Producers must therefore
leave `precision` un-laddered and set [`Self::magnitude_override`];
pre-applying it here AND setting the flag double-clamps the value.

Apply the legacy `OKTFormatter.changeUnique` magnitude override, which
keys on the RAW (pre-rounding) value: `< 1000` keeps `precision`;
`>= 1_000_000` forces `0`; otherwise `min(precision, 4)`.

Order amounts only. `false` for every other role — enabling it elsewhere
silently changes precision at magnitude boundaries.

This override is a case where the raw-string design is strictly closer to
legacy than a pre-formatted one: legacy keys on the raw value, which
native now has.

doc:
Formatting parameters for one display role (price, amount, fee, …).

Native applies this to an already-converted raw `String`:

```text
1. precision := magnitude_override ? change_unique(raw, precision) : precision
2. rounded   := round(raw, precision, rounding)
3. text      := trailing_zeros == Keep ? pad(rounded, precision) : strip(rounded)
4. text      := ICU(text, locale)                     // grouping, locale digits
5. text      := apply sign_type, then symbol/sign at unit_position
```

The render function must contain NO instrument, bot, or setting knowledge —
everything scenario-dependent is resolved into these fields by the Rust-side
factory.

`Default` is NOT a pass-through. It yields `precision: 0` + `Down`, and both
renderers apply `precision` as max-fraction-digits, so a defaulted convertor
TRUNCATES to an integer (`62183.45` -> `62,183`, `0.0035` -> `0`). It exists
only to make the struct constructible field-by-field.

So an unresolved instrument must be modelled as ABSENCE, never as a defaulted
convertor: carry `Option<…>` in state and let native keep its legacy
formatting until a real set arrives (see
`ContractDcaDetailState::convertors`). Precision 0 is a legitimate resolved
value for a contract size, so native cannot distinguish the two from the
number alone.

fields.doc:
Render this tag de-emphasised — the exact twin of
[`SpotGridOverviewTagPresentation::muted`], including the ANDROID-ONLY caveat; read that
field's doc for the full contract, which is not repeated here.

The one difference worth naming: the contract voucher chip is TAPPABLE
(`intent: Some(OpenVoucherRules)`, `enabled: true`) where spot's is inert, and muting does NOT
change that. Keeping the intent under `muted` is deliberate — styling and interactivity are
separate concerns, and this Record describes the RUST PRESENTATION, not the delivered UX.

DO NOT read that as "a muted chip still opens the rules sheet" — it does not, in any case where
this field is true. `muted` is only ever set when the voucher is expired AND the host is
onshore (`voucher_tag_is_muted`), and onshore is precisely where BOTH shipping clients block
the tap: Android skips the `singleClick` binding via `isLiteVoucherChip`
(`ContractGridOverviewFragment.kt:403`), and iOS disables the gesture recogniser via
`-[OKTNMPVoucherView shouldAllowTap]`, which returns `NO` whenever the app mode is Lite. So the
sheet is unreachable exactly when this field is true. The Rust-level tappability is pinned by
`a_muted_contract_voucher_chip_stays_tappable`, which is correct and asserts the presentation
only — it is not a claim about what the user can reach.

Defaulted so adding it does not break existing generated bindings or callers that predate it.

direction-derived tone as the direction chip, not a neutral one — so a short

axis; direction and leverage are appended unconditionally, which means a bot
with a blank or unrecognised direction, or a non-positive leverage, still
emits an EMPTY chip rather than none.

trade-unit preference. Native's equivalent is rebuilt on access because

doc:
One leg's `/max-available` row set, as the manual arbitrage KV panel needs it.

# Why RAW, and why the side selection is NOT baked in

Every field is the unconverted wire string. Two of the five displayed rows
("closable" and "position") are chosen by the leg's CURRENT direction at render
time, not at fetch time:

```text
closable = side == buy ? shortAvailablePos : longAvailablePos
position = side == buy ? shortPos          : longPos
```

(`OKTASPOKVInfoVC.m:150-155` — buying closes a SHORT, hence the inversion.)
Collapsing that here would freeze the choice against the side the request was
sent with, so a direction flip would show the other side's number for one
round-trip instead of the placeholder native shows.

# `fetched_side` is the staleness guard, not decoration

Native gates the whole panel on
`!currentSide || [currentSide isEqualToString:handler.side]`
(`OKTASPOKVInfoVC.m:143-148`), where `handler.side` is the side the commit
handler was CONSTRUCTED with (`OKTCommitOrderHandler.m:155-157` →
`_orderParams.side`). A direction change rebuilds the handler, so until the new
one lands the panel is showing a row that belongs to the previous direction, and
native prints `--` rather than a stale number.

Recording the side the request was sent with reproduces that exactly: the row is
renderable only while `fetched_side` still matches the leg's live side.

Native's sheet also passes an `instSymbol` key
(`OKTSSignalBotDetailInfoTabVC.m:212`), and callers currently reuse this
field for it. That reuse is WRONG — confirmed against native, so the
open question this doc used to carry is now settled the unfavourable
way:

* this field is the BASE coin alone. `get_trade_symbol()` is
`coin_format(inst_family).amount_sign.to_uppercase()`
(`core-trading/src/types/biz/futures_instrument.rs:309-313`) → `BTC`.
* `instSymbol` is base CONCATENATED with quote, plus a per-family
suffix. `OKTInstIDModel.m:133-149 (_setupInstSymbol)`:
swap/futures whose `instFamilyQuoteCcy` contains
`OKTInst_UM_UnderlyingFlag` (`"_"`, `OKTTypes.h:40`) →
`"<base><quote> <last _-component>"`; `instFamilyQuoteCcy ==
OKTFutureGroupTypeUSD` → `"<base><quote> CM"`
(`OKTInst_CM_EndDisplayFlag`, `OKTTypes.h:42`); everything else,
including SPOT and MARGIN → `"<base><quote>"`. So `BTC-USDT` → `BTCUSDT`.

The mini-program pair sheet therefore receives `BTC` where native sent
`BTCUSDT`. Deliberately NOT patched by composing
`get_trade_symbol() + get_quote_symbol()` here: that is right for SPOT
and USDT-margined SWAP but drops the UM/CM suffix, and core-trading is
read-only from this crate so the faithful accessor cannot be added
there. The composition rule above is recorded so a proper
`inst_symbol` field is a mechanical follow-up rather than a re-derivation.

producer [`project_instruments_with`] is unusable here for two reasons —
it gates on the place-order arm's `PairDataSource::enabled()`, and its
`metadata` REQUIRES a loaded hidden-currency wrapper. The detail warm-up
(`ensure_signal_bot_detail_trade_data_loaded`) loads SWAP + coins only, and
native's own pair sheet does no visibility filtering at all — it lists every
`signalFullInstIds` entry (`OKTSSignalBotDetailInfoTabVC.m:202-215`).
Requiring the hidden wrapper here would fail the whole sheet on a page that
never loads it.

fields.name: adopted_quote_ccy
fields.doc:
The pair quote currency `adopt_quote_ccy` last settled on; empty before
the first adoption.

Its only job is to tell a FIRST adoption from a later CHANGE, which is
what lets the snack bar fire on a mid-session quote switch
(`BTC-USD` → `BTC-USDT`) without also firing on plain page entry.

NOT what the order pays with — that is `trade_quote_ccy`, which an
acceptable quote deliberately leaves untouched. This one is written on
every adoption precisely because it is only a baseline for comparison,
so nothing downstream may read it as a currency to trade in.

fields.name: quote_ccy_switch_notice
fields.doc:
The currency an automatic switch landed on, when one happened.

Drives the dismissible snack bar (UI-13): recurring buy only accepts
USDT / USDC / USD, so entering the page in another currency — USDS
is the shipped case — switches to USDT and says so. `None` means
there is nothing to announce, either because no switch happened or
because the user dismissed the notice.

Durable state with an explicit `dismiss_quote_ccy_switch_notice`
rather than a one-shot event: the notice has to survive a rotation
or a backgrounding until the user actually dismisses it, which an
event cannot do.

fields.name: trade_quote_ccy_precision
fields.doc:
Decimal precision for `trade_quote_ccy`, set atomically with the ccy
via `set_trade_quote_ccy`. Native reads this to format balance display
without caching a separate snapshot that could drift from the ccy.
`None` until the first `set_trade_quote_ccy` call.

fields.name: selected_coins
fields.doc:
The basket being edited, in selection order. Rust owns this so the
coin picker, the allocation sheet, the minimum-investment lookup and
the order payload all read one list instead of three native
mirrors that can disagree.

fields.name: coin_ratio_total_percent
fields.doc:
Sum of [`Self::selected_coins`] ratios, in whole percent. Derived —
recomputed on every allocation mutation so native never has to.

fields.name: is_coin_allocation_valid
fields.doc:
Whether the basket can be submitted: between 1 and
[`MAX_SELECTED_COINS`] coins whose ratios sum to exactly 100.
Derived alongside [`Self::coin_ratio_total_percent`].

fields.name: recommend_id
fields.doc:
Popular Theme the user arrived from, when this page was opened by
accepting a recommendation. `None` for an ordinary manual creation.

Carried straight through to the order payload's optional
`recommendId` so the server can attribute the theme's cumulative
user count. It deliberately survives every other form edit: the
user is still creating *from* that theme even after retuning the
coins, amount or schedule, and losing it here silently
under-reports the theme.

fields.name: balances_error
fields.doc:
Raw upstream error from `fetch_account_balances`. Paired with
`balances_loading` (which acts as the loading sentinel for this
action — promoted to `ActionResultState` only when a caller need
for the typed FSM surfaces). Native composes localized UX copy.

fields.name: raw_total_balance
fields.doc: Sum of selected account balances (raw string for precision).

fields.name: min_investment_error
fields.doc:
Raw upstream error from the min-investment fetch; native composes
localized copy. There is no companion FSM field: the one that existed
belonged to `reload_min_investment`, a second, unused copy of this fetch,
and went with it.

fields.name: place_order_state
fields.doc:
Per-action FSM for `place_order`. Pairs with the existing
`place_order_error` (raw upstream string) +
`place_order_error_code` (server `sCode`) fields. Native reads
`place_order_state` for Loading/Success/Error transitions and
composes localized copy from the error string.

fields.name: place_order_error_code
fields.doc:
Server-side `sCode` when a business-error response is received
(`sCode != "0"`). `None` for transport errors. Always set together
with `place_order_error` so native can map both onto an NSError.

fields.name: inst_id
fields.doc:
Route instrument id, forwarded by native from the host Activity/nav args — plain route
identity, not a `core_trading` read.

fields.name: inst_type
fields.doc: Route instrument type — same provenance as `inst_id`.

fields.name: base_ccy
fields.doc:
Trade (base) symbol resolved from `core_trading` for `inst_id`, e.g. "BTC". `""` until
`resolve_identity` completes; native must not fall back to a locally computed value.

fields.name: identity_error
fields.doc:
Fatal `resolve_identity` failure (empty route id, `core_trading` preload failure, or
unknown instrument). Native has no equivalent business fallback for this — this is a
visible error state, not a deferred-retry signal.

fields.name: order_confirm_required
fields.doc:
Whether the order needs the secondary confirmation sheet.

Replaces native's `(instContext.trade.tradeSetting.confirm as NSString).boolValue ??
true`. Resolved from the ACCOUNT, not the instrument context, by
`get_order_remind_confirm_default_true()` — core-trading's own variant whose default
exists for exactly this reason ("confirm-ON is the safe default when the setting
cannot be resolved", added so a migrated panel would not flip the cold-launch
default).

Seeded `true` in [`seeded_initial_state`], NOT `false`: it is read at the moment the
user taps Create, which can precede `resolve_identity` completing, and the failure
this must not have is silently skipping a confirmation the user expects.

fields.name: resolution_generation
fields.doc:
Monotonic counter bumped once per `resolve_identity` call that actually proceeds (i.e.
clears state past the unchanged-instrument idempotency check below). Native gates its
identity-ready refresh chain on a generation change rather than `invest_ccy.isNotBlank()`
alone — `StateFlow` conflation can otherwise coalesce a genuine coin-switch's
blank->resolved transition away when the new instrument shares the old one's quote ccy.

fields.name: trade_quote_ccy_options
fields.doc:
Quote-currency choices resolved from the current `core_trading` instrument. Appended to
preserve the positional UniFFI record layout of every preceding field.
